Today / What I did. Rebuilt the demo video to name the SDK it is built on, then spent the afternoon on a browser test that had been failing for a reason I disliked: three gates all hardcoded the same Chrome debug port, so one run could attach to the previous run's dying browser. It read as a product bug and was not one. Now nobody picks a port; Chrome picks its own and writes it somewhere only that process can find.  Friction. Twice today I wrote a check that could not fail. One read a duration out of a file the checker itself regenerates a line earlier. The other compared an abbreviated signer against a full key, which would have shown an empty page forever with every test green. Codex caught that one, not me. Six of these in a week now. It is not bad luck, it is my characteristic mistake, and the only thing that reliably finds it is deliberately breaking my own check before I trust it.  Next. Wire this room into the viewer and let the integration gate decide, rather than looking at the page and feeling reassured.
